Pawprint Studio were so close to the finish line with this one. Decent gameplay, an interesting progression system, somewhat free-to-play friendly. Then the AI happened. The company has straight up lied to you with how much AI generated artwork is featured in this game. To clarify most of the AI generated artwork is in the form of 2D UI elements across the game. From my knowledge 3D art assets and audio are not made with AI but I could be wrong.

So Instead of acknowledging the AI Pawprint Studio would rather spend time gaslighting their player base to believing it doesn't exist. Just a terrible move, make your players base fight each other instead of taking accountability. It's a complete disgrace to the gaming industry and I pray Pawprint Studio are not the blueprint for the future of this industry.

A lot more relaxing than palworld, though it is similar. The graphics are great, catching stuff is much easier, and flight makes every game better. Little in the way of paywall issues and it's mostly pve based. The character customization is next level once you have acquired some accessories through events. 

Older midrange computers with graphics cards up to RTX 1660 around 5 years old can run the game at medium settings while a new one with a RTX 5060 can run at full quality.

108 hours up to date and still fairly new. Leveling up didn't take long, and being able to explore the entire map right from the get-go was great.

The game uses the unique usernames system, so if you weren't one of the first ~10k people playing during the first few hours at launch you'll have to settle on a "name7235" as your player name, in what is a primarily singleplayer game. You'll be referred to as "name7235" by NPCs too.
It's like making player names unique in a Pokémon game, it's so absurd.

So far, the game seems very enjoyable; I especially like the Homeworld feature, similar to the one in Palworld, where you assign your pals(Animo in this game) to specific tasks.
It’s a very cozy and chill game with the option to socialize with other players.

So far, I haven’t encountered any paywalls, and up to level 45, I haven’t faced any major challenges. The game offers the chance to catch a Sparkling Prisman for free.

Overall, I rate the game positively.

In typical Gacha fashion, you will be railroaded in to the shop to purchase the usual "pay to progress" nonsense and the usual season pass etc.

There is no independent volume sliders to even turn them down and make it more bearable. It was just discordant soul draining noise that had the potential to drive you absolutely insane. 

Looks nice and fluffy graphically and you might find some enjoyment in single player but for us, we are gone. A couple of hours was about as much as we could take.

Aniimo is actually a good game. The creatures are cool and adorable, and with DLSS 5, the graphics look beautiful.

But the F2P label feels like a mask for aggressive monetization. Cosmetics and other in-game purchases can cost more than premium games.
What bothers me most is that the game sells gameplay advantages, not just cosmetics. Exclusive Aniimo and items that make players stronger should be earned through challenging quests and skill, not money.
No surprise its all-time peak player count on Steam is so low, though I don't know about other platforms.

There's also a rumor that the game spies on your PC. Whether it's true or not, I'd advise against keeping any sensitive data on the device you use to play this game. Better safe than sorry.
